Paragraph: Summary of Passage: Lord Krishna notes that even intelligent people get confused when trying to distinguish between action and inaction, promising to reveal the true nature of action so Arjuna can be freed from misfortune.
Situation/Problem_Faced: The psychological and philosophical confusion regarding what constitutes meaningful, constructive action versus passive non-action.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna states: 'kim karma kim akarmeti kavayo 'py atra mohitah, tat te karma pravaksyami yaj jnatva moksyase 'subhat' (Even the wise are confused about what is action and inaction; I will explain action to you so you can be freed from ill fortune).
Outcome/Resolution: Clears cognitive ambiguity surrounding duty, preparing Arjuna to discern true right action from mere activity.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Cognitive Clarity: Gaining clear mental vision free from confusion or self-doubt
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Overcoming Decision Paralysis: Resolving hesitation when faced with complex behavioral choices
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Understanding Intentionality: Recognizing that the inner motive shapes the nature of an action

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Kim karma kim akarmeti (What is action and what is inaction)
Kavayo 'py atra mohitah (Even the intelligent/wise are bewildered)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Discernment between spiritualized action and spiritual inaction is subtle; receiving divine guidance liberates the soul from material bondage.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Mental confusion about choices leads to paralysis; clarifying your core intentions restores decisiveness and reduces internal anxiety.
